content: chrome.storage.session is in-memory only (1MB quota default), cleared when the browser session terminates (not necessarily on every SW idle-kill - the SW itself is what gets killed/restarted, storage.session survives SW restarts within the same browser session). No native TTL/expiry - any auto-lock timeout must be implemented by the extension itself (e.g. chrome.alarms) checking a stored timestamp, not relied upon from the storage API.
